en.bdb: Especiality of the Sikh of Guru

verses.gurmukhi: ਚੰਦਨ ਵਾਸੁ ਵਣਾਸਪਤਿ ਬਾਵਨ ਚੰਦਨਿ ਚੰਦਨੁ ਹੋਈ।
verses.translit_en: cha(n)dhan vaas vanaasapat baavan cha(n)dhan cha(n)dhan hoiee|

en.bdb: With the fragrance of sandalwood the whole vegetation becomes sandal.

verses.gurmukhi: ਫਲ ਵਿਣੁ ਚੰਦਨੁ ਬਾਵਨਾ ਆਦਿ ਅਨਾਦਿ ਬਿਅੰਤੁ ਸਦੋਈ।
verses.translit_en: fal vin cha(n)dhan baavanaa aadh anaadh bia(n)t sadhoiee|

en.bdb: Though itself the sandal is without fruit but it is always considered as costly.

verses.gurmukhi: ਚੰਦਨੁ ਬਾਵਨ ਚੰਦਨਹੁ ਚੰਦਨ ਵਾਸੁ ਨ ਚੰਦਨੁ ਕੋਈ।
verses.translit_en: cha(n)dhan baavan cha(n)dhanahu cha(n)dhan vaas na cha(n)dhan koiee|

en.bdb: But the plant, which becomes sandal through the fragrance of sandal, cannot make any other plant sandal.

verses.gurmukhi: ਅਸਟੁ ਧਾਤੁ ਇਕੁ ਧਾਤੁ ਹੋਇ ਪਾਰਸ ਪਰਸੇ ਕੰਚਨੁ ਜੋਈ।
verses.translit_en: asaT dhaat ik dhaat hoi paaras parase ka(n)chan joiee|

en.bdb: Eight metals touching the philosopher’s stone becomes gold but that gold cannot produce further gold.

verses.gurmukhi: ਕੰਚਨ ਹੋਇ ਨ ਕੰਚਨਹੁ ਵਰਤਮਾਨ ਵਰਤੈ ਸਭਿ ਲੋਈ।
verses.translit_en: ka(n)chan hoi na ka(n)chanahu varatamaan varatai sabh loiee|

en.bdb: All this is performed in the present only (but the Sikh of Guru makes many like himself; they further become competent to transform others into a Sikh way of life).

verses.gurmukhi: ਨਦੀਆ ਨਾਲੇ ਗੰਗ ਸੰਗਿ ਸਾਗਰ ਸੰਗਮਿ ਖਾਰਾ ਸੋਈ।
verses.translit_en: nadheeaa naale ga(n)g sa(n)g saagar sa(n)gam khaaraa soiee|

en.bdb: Rivers, streams and even the Ganges become brackish in the company of ocean.

verses.gurmukhi: ਬਗੁਲਾ ਹੰਸੁ ਨ ਹੋਵਈ ਮਾਨਸਰੋਵਰਿ ਜਾਇ ਖਲੋਈ।
verses.translit_en: bagulaa ha(n)s na hoviee maanasarovar jai khaloiee|

en.bdb: The crane never becomes swan even if it sits at Manasarovar.
It so happens because an ordinary person remains always involved in the counts of twenties and more i.e. money.
